official.deadline_note: Official AY 2026-27 timeline: A2A portal open to students 27 February - 22 April 2026; universities scrutinize and upload provisional admission confirmations 27 February - 31 May 2026; Indian Missions select 27 February - 15 June 2026 with a second round 15 - 30 June 2026; indicative joining June - August 2026. Bangladesh applicants must register at sjsdhaka.gov.in before the A2A portal.
official.application_cycle: ICCR Scholarship Programme 2026-27 (Academic Year 2026-27); 500 slots allocated to the Suborno Jayanti Scholarship Scheme for Bangladesh nationals
official.status_note: The official AY 2026-27 timeline lists the student application window as 27 February to 22 April 2026, which has closed. The A2A portal still lists 2026-27 as the registration year and carries the notice 'Please contact the Indian Mission for any scholarship updates'; the sjsdhaka.gov.in site still displays the earlier A.Y 2025-26 closing date of 30 April 2025.
official.tuition_coverage_note: ICCR scheme page, Facilities: 'Tuition fee/OCF paid to Universities (Norms attached)' alongside Stipend, HRA, Contingent Allowances, Thesis/Dissertation Allowance and Airfare.
benefits: Monthly House Rent Allowance: INR 6,500 (Grade I cities) / INR 5,500 (other cities) - printed on the UG row of the official allowances table; the PG and Ph.D. rows share one merged HRA cell with no printed figure
Annual Contingent Allowance: INR 5,000 (UG) / INR 7,000 (PG) / INR 12,500 (Ph.D.)
One-time thesis/dissertation allowance: *INR 7,000 (UG and PG) / INR 10,000 (Ph.D.); *only applicable where a Project Report is a prescribed course requirement
Return economy-class airfare to the airport nearest the place of study, plus 3-tier AC train fare within India if required
Tuition fee/OCF paid directly to the universities under attached norms
eligibility: 18 years minimum age for any level of courses, as on 1 July of the academic year (1 July 2026)
35 years maximum age for UG, PG, Certificate and Diploma level courses, as on 1 July 2026
40 years maximum age for Ph.D. level courses, as on 1 July 2026
Passport with a minimum validity of two years as on 1 July 2026
Applicants must possess proficiency in English - foreign students' classes are conducted in English
Prohibited streams: Medical, Law and Integrated courses; scheme restricted to Bangladesh nationals (500 slots, STEM and Non-STEM 50% each)
requirements: Mandatory essay of 500 words in English on one of the topics listed on the A2A Portal
English proficiency must be proved to the standard determined by the Indian Mission; TOEFL/IELTS certificates may be uploaded as additional proof
Ph.D. applicants must submit a synopsis of the research topic along with the application
Medical health insurance with minimum cover of INR 500,000, taken at the student's own expense, is a mandatory prerequisite for receiving scholarship allowances
documents: Passport with minimum two years' validity as on 1 July 2026, plus passport-size photograph on a white background with both ears visible
SSC/HSC or equivalent mark sheets and transcripts in English; notarized English translation if issued in another language
Certified copy of the transcript/syllabus of the last qualifying examination
500-word English essay composed on the A2A Portal; TOEFL/IELTS certificates if available
Medical health insurance policy with minimum INR 500,000 sum assured
AIU Equivalence Certificate if applicable; research synopsis for Ph.D.; Joining Report Form from the A2A portal after selection
selection_criteria: Selection of candidates is the sole discretion of the Indian Mission; the Mission and ICCR reserve the right to accept or reject any application at any stage without assigning any reason
Universities/Institutions scrutinize applications and upload provisional admission confirmations; the Mission selects candidates against the slots allocated to the country
Grant of admission by one or more universities does not guarantee the award of scholarship; only admission confirmations routed through the A2A portal count
coverage: Monthly stipend for living expenses (INR 18,000 / 20,000 / 22,000 by level)
Monthly House Rent Allowance (INR 6,500 Grade I cities / INR 5,500 other cities, as printed)
Annual contingent grant and one-time thesis/dissertation allowance for eligible courses
Return economy-class airfare and 3-tier AC train fare within India
Hostel/mess charges, security deposits, FRRO registration and other fees outside the norms remain payable by the student
application_method: Step 1: Register at the Suborno Jayanti Portal (https://sjsdhaka.gov.in) - ICCR's official notice instructs Bangladesh applicants to register here FIRST
Step 2: Register on the A2A Portal (https://a2ascholarships.iccr.gov.in) and complete the application, including the 500-word essay
Universities scrutinize the application and upload provisional admission confirmation on the A2A portal
The Indian Mission/Post selects candidates against the country's allocated slots and issues the offer letter via the portal
official.application_route: Two-step online route for Bangladesh nationals: register on sjsdhaka.gov.in first, then on a2ascholarships.iccr.gov.in; applications made only on A2A without the SJS step are rejected.
official.study_mode: Full-time structured courses of one year or more at UG, PG and Ph.D. level (Certificate/Diploma only in Indian languages/literature, performing/visual arts and yoga)
official.citizenship_residency: Bangladesh nationals only under the Suborno Jayanti Scholarship Scheme, which subsumes all earlier ICCR schemes for Bangladesh
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scheme is exclusively for foreign (Bangladeshi) nationals
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All fields except Medicine/Paramedical (nursing, physiotherapy, anaesthesia), Fashion, Law and integrated 5-year programmes such as BA-LLB/BSc-MSc; 500 slots split STEM / Non-STEM 50% each
official.research_requirement: Ph.D. applicants must submit a synopsis of the research topic with the application; research-level admission is available only at Ph.D. level
official.duration: Scholarships only for structured courses of one year or more; prescribed tenure for a regular Ph.D. student is 3 years, extendable at ICCR's discretion in blocks of up to six months to a maximum of two years, with no stipend paid for viva-voce extension
official.description: Under the Suborno Jayanti Scholarship Scheme, as ICCR states, scholarships to Bangladesh nationals are offered under one scheme 'subsuming all other schemes under which scholarships were being offered till now', with 500 slots at UG, PG and Ph.D. level in Indian universities, funded by the Government of India through ICCR and administered through the A2A portal in coordination with Indian Missions.
official.program_type: Government scholarship (ICCR, Ministry of External Affairs) - 500 seats for Bangladesh under Suborno Jayanti
official.english_requirement: Classes for foreign students are conducted in English; applicants must prove English proficiency to the standard set by the Indian Mission and must submit a mandatory 500-word essay in English on a topic listed on the A2A Portal; TOEFL/IELTS scores may be uploaded as additional proof but do not replace the essay

not_confirmed: Monthly House Rent Allowance for PG and Ph.D. levels - the official allowances table prints HRA figures only on the UG row, with the PG/Ph.D. HRA cells merged and blank
Whether the A2A portal still accepts new 2026-27 student applications after the 22 April 2026 deadline - the portal notice directs applicants to their Indian Mission
Number of university preferences allowed per application - not stated on the official pages checked
verification.notes: Stipend, HRA, contingent and thesis amounts were read from Section 15 'Scholarship Allowances' of the official Policy Guidelines PDF hosted on the ICCR A2A portal for AY 2026-27 (rendered table image checked cell by cell); deadline and process dates from the official 'Revised Timelines' PDF; slots, streams, airfare and facilities from the iccr.gov.in scheme page. Current age limits (18 min / 35 max UG-PG / 40 max PhD as on 1 July 2026) supersede older 18-30 and under-45 versions still quoted in some summaries.

applicant_utility.summary: This is the Government of India route for Bangladeshi students to study in India: 500 seats per year covering UG, PG and PhD at empanelled universities, with tuition paid straight to the university, a monthly stipend of INR 18,000-22,000 depending on level, house rent allowance, annual contingent and thesis allowances, and return economy airfare. The 2026-27 application window ran from 27 February to 22 April 2026, so timing now depends on the next cycle announced through the High Commission of India, Dhaka. Applicants must register on the Suborno Jayanti portal (sjsdhaka.gov.in) before touching the A2A portal - skipping that first step is a known cause of outright rejection. No IELTS is needed to compete: the mandatory 500-word essay written inside the A2A portal is the standard English test.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Bangladeshi nationals with strong SSC/HSC or degree marks who want a funded UG, PG or PhD place in India and have no IELTS score.
application_readiness_checklist: Create the sjsdhaka.gov.in login first and complete it before starting the A2A registration
Secure or renew a passport valid for at least two years beyond 1 July of the academic year
Collect mark sheets and transcripts and arrange notarized English translations where they are not in English; Ph.D. applicants prepare the research synopsis in the same pass
Draft and practice the 500-word English essay on an A2A-listed topic before the portal opens
Buy medical insurance with at least INR 5,00,000 sum assured - allowances are blocked without it
Budget roughly USD 1,500 for initial settlement, since allowances start only after joining formalities and a local bank account are completed (about 2-3 months)
common_rejection_risks: Registering only on A2A without the mandatory Suborno Jayanti portal registration
Passport validity shorter than two years as on 1 July of the academic year
Crossing the age ceiling on 1 July - 35 for UG/PG, 40 for PhD
Applying for a prohibited stream (medicine, nursing, fashion, law, integrated five-year degrees)
Documents uploaded without English translation or a notarized translation where required
Expecting stipend on arrival - allowances are released only after the certified joining report and bank formalities, about 2-3 months in
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Hostel or private accommodation and mess charges, security deposits and caution money, FRRO/immigration registration and penalties, certificate and registration fees, the medical insurance premium, the roughly USD 1,500 initial settlement advised before first allowance, and excess baggage on the funded airfare.
document_audit: The 500-word essay is written and submitted inside the A2A portal - it is not a separate upload, and TOEFL/IELTS cannot substitute for it
The passport photo must be passport-size, white background, both ears visible, per A2A specifications
Transcripts of the last qualifying examination must be certified copies; non-English originals need notarized translations
PhD synopsis must accompany the application itself, and admission to research courses exists only at PhD level
After selection, the Joining Report Form from the A2A portal, visa upload and physical/medical fitness format come into play - keep originals of every uploaded document
alerts: Allowances depend on academic progress - failing to be promoted stops stipend and HRA until the backlog is cleared
Staying outside India more than 30 continuous days cuts the stipend by 50%; beyond 60 days all allowances except HRA are deducted
The scholarship covers only the awarded individual - no family members are funded financially
Conduct rules are strict and explicitly cover social media; violations can lead to termination and deportation
Selection rests entirely with the Indian Mission and no reasons are communicated; admission alone is not a scholarship
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register at sjsdhaka.gov.in, then at a2ascholarships.iccr.gov.in, complete the form, essay and uploads by 22 April; universities then upload provisional admission confirmations, the Indian Mission selects against allocated slots and issues the offer letter through the A2A portal.

official.deadline_note: No central deadline: each of the 149 listed programmes sets its own application deadline in its Call for Applications. Deadlines are updated annually in the second quarter; the flagship 'Study Scholarships - Master Studies for All Academic Disciplines' programme accepts applications between 1 June and its stated deadline, and its portal closes at 24:00 CET/CEST on the final day.
official.application_cycle: Rolling per programme; funding cycles are stated in each Call for Applications (e.g. the flagship Master's programme: applications 1 June onward, funding must begin in 2027, usually starting 1 October 2027)
official.status_note: The DAAD scholarship database is live with 149 scholarship options (checked 10 October 2026). Individual programme portals open and close on their own schedules - the flagship Master's programme currently shows 'Currently you cannot apply for this programme' between its 1 June opening and next deadline.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Official FAQ section F.7: 'DAAD does not pay tuition fees for its scholarship holders'; the flagship programme page repeats that the DAAD does not cover tuition fees.
benefits: Monthly scholarship payment: EUR 992 for Master's students; EUR 1,400 for doctoral candidates and postdocs (rates for university teachers: EUR 2,000 assistant teachers/lecturers, EUR 2,150 professors)
Payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance cover in many programmes
Flat-rate travel allowance (in some programmes upon application only)
One-off research or annual study allowance where provided (e.g. EUR 460 annual study allowance in the flagship Master's programme)

Programme-dependent extras: monthly rent subsidy on application, monthly partner allowance of EUR 276, child allowance of EUR 259 per child, disability/illness top-up, and Green Mobility top-up for climate-friendly travel
Language support: funded German course (2, 4 or 6 months) where required, online language course fees, and TestDaF/DSH fee reimbursement
eligibility: Aimed primarily at graduates, doctoral students and postdocs for study and research visits in Germany
No fixed age limit in most programmes; as a rule the most recent degree should not date back more than six years at the application deadline
Full-time study or research with compulsory attendance in Germany - distance, online, part-time and dual programmes are not eligible
Applicants must not have been resident in Germany for longer than 15 months at the application deadline
A DAAD scholarship cannot be combined with another scholarship from DAAD or another German funding organisation at the same time
Country and status eligibility are set per programme - filter by country of origin/residence in the database
requirements: Proof of current proficiency in the language of instruction (German, English or both), with certificates no older than three years
For individual research or doctorate: a letter confirming academic supervision from a German host, plus a research proposal with a separately uploaded time plan
Applications must be submitted within the programme's own window, online through the DAAD portal
Master's applicants arrange their own university admission; a DAAD award letter is only valid together with admission to the named university
documents: Online application form in the DAAD portal
Curriculum vitae in tabular form (max. 3 pages)
Letter of motivation, 1-3 pages, on academic and personal reasons for the planned project
Current transcript of records and university degree certificate (degree certificate may follow before funding starts)
One recent supporting letter of recommendation from a university teacher (form generated in the DAAD portal)
Language certificate for the language of instruction (under 3 years old); German/English translations of any documents in other languages; research proposal and separate time plan for research grants
selection_criteria: Professional qualification: academic achievements and progress, course of studies, language knowledge, relevant internships or work experience
Quality of the study or research project: quality and preparation, choice of programme and host, feasibility and consistency of the work plan, integration into the academic career path
Potential of the applicant: motivation, prospects of the stay for further development, extracurricular commitment
Equal opportunity: special circumstances such as disability, chronic illness, childcare, caring for relatives or refugee background are considered to compensate disadvantages
Independent selection committees of university teachers and researchers decide; DAAD staff have no vote
coverage: Monthly stipend towards living costs (EUR 992 Master's; EUR 1,400 doctoral/postdoc)
Health, accident and personal liability insurance in many programmes
Programme-dependent allowances: study/research allowance, rent subsidy, family and childcare allowances, disability top-up
Tuition fees are explicitly not covered - DAAD does not pay tuition, and DAAD notes the stipend will not always cover all living expenses, especially in high-rent university towns
application_method: Find the programme in the DAAD scholarship database, filtering by country, status, purpose and subject
Read the Call for Applications in full: eligibility, deadline, application procedure and required documents
Register in the DAAD portal and generate the letter-of-recommendation form there during the application period
Complete the online application and upload all listed documents as PDFs before the programme deadline; the portal closes at 24:00 CET/CEST on the last day
official.application_route: No central application - select a programme in the DAAD scholarship database and submit through that programme's DAAD portal window (some programmes use direct submission to a stated address).
official.study_mode: Full-time study or research with compulsory attendance in Germany; distance, online, blended and part-time programmes are not funded
official.citizenship_residency: Apply from your country of origin or current country of residence; dual nationals apply from their country of origin and may not apply from two countries at once; maximum 15 months' residence in Germany at the deadline
official.international_eligibility: Yes - programmes are aimed at international students and researchers; eligible countries differ per programme and are selectable in the database
official.research_requirement: Research grants require a detailed proposal (max. 10 pages unless stated otherwise) agreed with the academic supervisor plus a separately uploaded time plan; individual doctorates additionally require the letter confirming academic supervision
official.duration: Set per programme in its Call for Applications - e.g. the flagship Master's programme funds visits of 10 to 24 months, and the EPOS postgraduate programme funds 12 to 42 months
official.description: DAAD describes itself as the world's largest funding organisation of its kind, supporting well over 100,000 German and international students and researchers around the globe every year; its scholarships are aimed primarily at graduates, doctoral students and postdocs for study and research visits to universities and non-university research institutions in Germany, and do not have to be paid back.
official.program_type: Scholarship database - 149 DAAD and partner funding programmes listed (checked 10 October 2026), each with its own eligibility, deadline and benefits
official.english_requirement: Proof of proficiency in the language of instruction is mandatory: for English-taught programmes e.g. TOEFL iBT/TOEIC/PTE/IELTS/Duolingo English Test/onSET (certificate under 3 years old); no English proof required from applicants from Australia, Canada (except Quebec), Ireland, New Zealand, Singapore, the UK or the USA; for German-taught programmes e.g. TestDaF, DSH, Goethe-Zertifikat, waived for applicants from Austria and Switzerland

not_confirmed: A central deadline - none exists, each of the 149 programmes sets its own, so no single date can be recorded
Programme-specific GPA cut-offs - DAAD states programmes as a rule stipulate no minimum grade point average, leaving exact thresholds to each Call
verification.notes: Monthly rates read from the official FAQ for scholarship applicants (section F.1: EUR 992 Master's, EUR 1,400 doctoral/postdoc); tuition exclusion from FAQ F.7 and the flagship programme page; insurance, travel, family benefits from FAQ F.2-F.4; the DAAD overview page still shows the older EUR 1,300 doctoral figure, while the applicant FAQ states EUR 1,400 (effective February 2026) - the FAQ figure was recorded.

applicant_utility.summary: Treat DAAD as a catalogue, not a single scholarship: 149 funding programmes sit in its database, and you apply to one specific programme whose Call for Applications decides your eligibility, deadline and benefits - a central DAAD application does not exist. Expect EUR 992 a month at Master's level or EUR 1,400 as a doctoral candidate, plus insurance, a flat-rate travel allowance and possible family or rent top-ups, but plan your own money for tuition and any rent gap, because DAAD states plainly that it does not pay tuition fees and that the stipend will not always cover all living expenses. Bangladeshi applicants should filter the database by Bangladesh and lean on the DAAD Information Centre Dhaka for advice and web sessions.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Graduates and researchers with a specific, well-prepared project, strong transcripts and a convincing motivation letter - not applicants hoping one generic DAAD form will find them money.
application_readiness_checklist: Shortlist programmes in the database by country, status (Graduates/PhD students/PhD holders/Lecturers), purpose and subject
Read each chosen Call for Applications end to end, especially application procedure, required documents and the country-specific notes
Confirm your language certificate is under three years old and matches the language of instruction
For research or PhD programmes, email potential German supervisors early and secure the letter confirming academic supervision plus an agreed proposal

Register on the DAAD portal when the window opens (the flagship Master's programme opens 1 June), generate the recommendation form inside the portal, upload everything as PDF, and submit at least a day early - the portal closes at 24:00 CET/CEST on the deadline day
Arrange your own university admission application in parallel - a DAAD award without admission to the named university is void
common_rejection_risks: Submitting an incomplete file - DAAD states incomplete applications cannot be considered and completeness is the applicant's responsibility
Applying to a programme whose eligible-country list does not include your country
An expired (over three years old) or mismatched language certificate for the language of instruction
A thin motivation letter or an unagreed, generic research proposal with no feasible timetable
Assuming tuition is funded - fee-charging locations such as Baden-Wuerttemberg (EUR 1,500 per semester for non-EU students) or TUM (EUR 4,000-6,000 per semester) will burn a self-funded budget
Holding another German state scholarship, which cannot run alongside a DAAD scholarship
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees where charged, semester contributions, rent above the EUR 992/1,400 monthly stipend in expensive cities, language test fees (not reimbursed unless TestDaF/DSH after award), certified translations where required, and pre-departure and visa costs.
document_audit: The letter of motivation is capped at 1-3 pages and must state academic and personal reasons - a recycled statement of purpose is easy to spot
The research proposal's time plan must be uploaded as a separate document, not appended inside the proposal
Non-German/English documents need translations, but scans do not have to be certified unless DAAD asks after a positive decision
The supervisor letter should confirm the project was discussed, a workplace exists and state the working language - generic emails weaken the file
Use a desktop computer for the portal; DAAD warns mobile access is only partially possible, and PDF is the only accepted upload format
alerts: Apply from the right country: dual nationals apply from their country of origin, and you may not hold simultaneous applications from two countries
Any extra income above EUR 603 gross a month is deducted from the stipend, and a second scholarship from a German state source cannot be combined
Deadlines are refreshed in the second quarter of each year, so last year's date is a guide, not a promise
If the DAAD-insured health cover is essential, note listed pre-existing conditions (e.g. HIV, MS, cancer, haemophilia, chronic kidney disease) are excluded - contact DAAD before you start
DAAD Bangladesh runs free web sessions (e.g. Bachelor's, Master's, PhD sessions in October 2026) that are the cheapest way to check your fit before applying
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Pick a programme in the database, then register in the DAAD portal during its window, generate the recommendation form, fill in the online application and upload the Call's documents as PDFs, and submit before the programme's deadline (portal closes 24:00 CET/CEST on the final day).
